summary: Only one live agent may declare `handles-faults`. Publishing a second holder is refused with `fault-agent-taken`, so the flag moves only by stopping its holder or dropping it there; when two members each accepted a different holder, neither is the fleet's fault agent until one steps down. A fault dismissal now hides a fault only when a person wrote it, or the agent that held `handles-faults` when it was written

replay.detail: No replay change; the fault agent and dismissed faults are still derived from the graph on each read.

schema.detail: No claim kind, field or database change.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: A publication that declares a second live `handles-faults` holder is refused (`fault-agent-taken`); one that declares no holder is never refused. A member on an older build still takes the first holder by subject, and still honours a dismissal from any actor, until it runs this build.

downtime.detail: No startup work or expected interruption.

manual.detail: Moving the fault agent to a new seat or a new run now means stopping the old holder first (or ending its run, or dropping `handles-faults` from it in the same publication); otherwise the new declaration is refused with `fault-agent-taken`. The fleet declares one holder today, so nothing needs doing at the roll.

recovery.detail: No additional recovery procedure introduced by this change. Preserve graph state, keys and configuration and follow the standard roll-forward guidance; this note does not qualify binary-only downgrade of the whole release.
